prompt: What is recursion, and what must every recursive function have?

rubric.referenceAnswer: Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version of the same problem. Every recursive function needs a base case that returns without another call, otherwise it never stops and the call stack overflows. Typical examples are factorial and walking a tree.

criteria.description: A function calls itself on a smaller instance of the same problem
It needs a base case that stops the recursion
Without a base case the call stack overflows
Gives a typical example such as factorial, Fibonacci or tree traversal
Uses the terms base case and call stack

misconceptions: Recursion is just a loop and is always faster than iteration
A recursive function does not need a stopping condition
